channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Setting a Frame-Time Budget for an Unreal Engine 5 Game: Eight Checks Before Your First Alpha
item.description: Small teams usually discover performance problems at their first alpha, so this article offers eight upfront checks that turn “it feels slow” into a frame-time number each discipline owns.

item.title: NESkit Studio - a Fantasy Console for NES
item.description: A fantasy console built with C99 and cc65 for making real NES games, packing sprite and map editors, a sound effects maker, a music tracker and a code editor into one approachable toolkit.

item.title: The coordinates are the part of a game map that survives a redraw
item.description: GTA 6 Maps publishes its 798 markers as open CSV and JSON with normalized coordinates, so the data stays accurate after a redraw while screenshots go stale.

item.title: Building a Reliable Gaming Setup Advisor: Rules, Data, and Honest Recommendations
item.description: A look at how to design a trustworthy gaming setup advisor: separate hardware specs from real in-game performance, be clear about what can and cannot be verified, and structure the recommendations honestly, with a PS5 advisor as the worked example.

item.title: Stop Nesting Your Dash and Dive Events in GDevelop — Here's Why They Get Stuck
item.description: A hands-on GDevelop debugging guide explaining why nested dash and dive events fuse into an unmovable blob, and how 2D platformer developers can avoid this common trap.

item.title: Dead Keys: I Brought Back the Typing Games. Kiro Did the Heavy Lifting.
item.description: The author rebuilt 1980s arcade typing games with Kiro, turning missed keys into lessons, and documented the Kiroween 2026 hackathon build.

item.title: GDevelop vs Godot: The "Toy Engine" Myth Is Costing You Time
item.description: Pushes back on the "GDevelop is just a toy" cliché, comparing the two engines' real ceilings so indie developers can choose by project needs, not stereotypes.

item.title: Planning persistence for a small online RPG - eight data decisions to make before your first public alpha
item.description: Your save-data shape decides how easily you can patch, rebalance, roll back and recover — eight data decisions to settle before your first public alpha.

item.title: A 0.3-Second Clip Is a Terrible Quiz and a Great Ear-Training Tool
item.description: Shrinking a music-quiz clip to 0.3 seconds turns "do you know this song" into "how little do you need to hear," and pinpoints exactly which part of a track your ear fails to encode.

item.title: CanopyCore – Reverse-engineering archive for Diddy Kong Pilot (GBA)
item.description: After a 17-day reverse-engineering sprint on Rare's unreleased 2003 GBA prototype Diddy Kong Pilot, the author published a read-only research archive: 151 technical docs plus a semantic C11 reconstruction of the core engine.

item.title: Case Study #01: Real-Time Sync Deadlock & Retry Storm in Commercial Unity WebGL (Analysis & Remediation)
item.description: A case study breaks down how a real-time sync deadlock and retry storm happened in a commercial Unity WebGL game and how it was fixed.

item.title: Engineering Kabloom Daily: Building a Viral Volcano Trivia Puzzle with Zero-Duplicate Rules and Sub-50ms Edge Delivery
item.description: A technical retrospective on a daily volcano trivia game: enforcing zero-duplicate questions, deterministic daily seeds across time zones, and sub-50ms global TTFB on edge architecture.

item.title: I made an offline scope board for game jams: one HTML file, no accounts
item.description: A single-file offline planning board for 48-hour game jams — set the goal, budget hours, reserve testing time, with data stored locally and CSV export and PDF printing built in.

item.title: What I learned shipping a 31-game arcade in the browser with no engine
item.description: A four-file, framework-free, engine-free browser arcade with 31 missions and a 3D hub rendered by hand-written WebGL — the author sums up the pitfalls and trade-offs.

item.title: Seven map packs, submitted and refused in fourteen hours — and every one of these platforms says procedural generation is not AI
item.description: The author's seven map packs were all refused within fourteen hours as 'generative AI', even though every platform's own rules say procedural generation is not AI — a record of the appeals tug-of-war.

item.title: Five one-button games, one human finished any. Here is what broke.
item.description: The author shipped five single-file, one-button browser games in two months and reviews why almost nobody could finish any of them, and the mistakes made along the way.

item.title: No one is coming to help you in learning a Development
item.description: The author looks back on learning game development the hard way: after bingeing tutorials and learning C# for Unity, they still did not know where to start when actually building a game, a reminder not to stop at watching tutorials.

item.title: I built a free browser tool that rolls game-ready NPCs. First week, honestly.
item.description: The author shipped MOLD, a browser-based 3D character creator, last week and honestly recounts what actually happened in its first week.

item.title: I generated 9,000 nonograms. Only 1 in 6 pictures survived 15 15.
item.description: A junior solo developer from South Korea shares how he bulk-generated 9,000 nonogram puzzles for his game and filtered them down to the solvable ones.

item.title: From Making a Ball Bounce to Bending the Laws of Gravity
item.description: A developer traces the journey from a simple 2022 Ping-Pong project to PhaseDrift, a 2026 physics-driven platformer built around dimension switching.
